problems: stop 1 card 4, answer 2: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: David opens the song by saying, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). When that shepherd is leading the way, you are completely covered.
David doesn't say he earns it. He says the LORD is his shepherd, and because of that, he lacks nothing (Psalm 23:1).
The text doesn't mention losing anything. David's point right at the start is that with the LORD as his shepherd, he shall not want (Psalm 23:1).
Green pastures and quiet waters paint a picture of deep rest. The LORD makes David lie down right there in the grass (Psalm 23:2).
That is not the vibe here at all. The LORD makes him lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters, which is pure rest (Psalm 23:2).
Danger shows up later in the psalm, but not here. Right now it is quiet waters and green grass where the sheep can finally relax (Psalm 23:2).
David tells us that the LORD "restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). His care goes way beyond grass and water straight to the inside.
The text doesn't say the LORD tests his soul here. It says He restores it, bringing back what was worn down (Psalm 23:3).
The verse doesn't talk about weighing souls. David says the LORD "restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3).

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: David says the LORD guides him in the right paths "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). It is about who the shepherd is.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: The flock benefits, but that is not the reason David gives. He says the guide happens "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3).

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention the land here. David writes that the LORD guides him "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3).

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: David isn't shaking in his boots in that dark valley because he knows "You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). The shepherd stays right there.
David doesn't credit his own strength. He says he fears no evil because "You are with me" (Psalm 23:4).
The text doesn't say how long the valley is. David's courage comes from one thing: "for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4).
David says straight out that "Your rod and your staff, they comfort me" even in the valley of the shadow of death (Psalm 23:4).
It is definitely true. David explicitly writes that the rod and the staff bring him comfort right there in the dark valley (Psalm 23:4).
The scene shifts to a feast, and David says, "You prepare a table before me" (Psalm 23:5). The host pulls out all the stops.
The text doesn't mention a tent. David says the LORD prepares a table before him (Psalm 23:5).
A bed was earlier with the green pastures, but here at the feast the LORD prepares a table (Psalm 23:5).
The text actually says the opposite of far away, because the table is set "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5).
You got it, baker. The table isn't hidden away. The LORD prepares it right "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5).
When David says "my cup overflows," he means the blessing doesn't just stop at the rim (Psalm 23:5). He has more than enough.
Spilling a drink by being careless is one thing, but an overflowing cup here means overflowing generosity and blessing from the host (Psalm 23:5).
Nobody is rushing this meal. An overflowing cup is a picture of total abundance at the table (Psalm 23:5).
David looks out across his whole life and says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6).
The text doesn't mention wealth and honor following him. David specifically names goodness and mercy (Psalm 23:6).
Those are great things to have, but the song says "goodness and mercy" will follow him all his days (Psalm 23:6).

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: David finishes his song by saying, "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). That is where the road leads.
Hebron was where David ruled as king for a time, but that is not where he says he will dwell forever. He says "in the house of the LORD" (Psalm 23:6).
Canaan was the promised land, but David's final destination in the song is "in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6).
